card: Removes time-based transaction expiry (-mempoolexpiry) and drops the mempool's entry_time index. Age-based eviction is incentive-incompatible because it discards transactions that are still mineable, such as low-feerate parents waiting for CPFP bumps. Dropping the index also saves memory overhead per transaction entry, fitting slightly more transactions into the configured -maxmempool budget. The -mempoolexpiry option is kept as a hidden no-op that logs a warning.
evidence: Fixes issue #33510: 'Mempool Expiry eviction might remove txs that could be mined in the next block'.
PR description and commit d40e511d9d note that age-based eviction 'can drop still-mineable transactions, such as a low-feerate parent waiting on a fee-bumping child.'

PR description notes that dropping the index removes one ordered-tree node per entry, lowering per-entry DynamicMemoryUsage() overhead so the mempool fits more transactions within the same -maxmempool budget.
problem: Evicting transactions based purely on age (previously defaulting to two weeks) is incentive-incompatible: it can drop transactions that could still be mined, such as a low-feerate parent awaiting a fee-bumping child. Maintaining the entry_time index also incurs an ordered-tree node of memory overhead per mempool entry.

risk.why: Mistakes in mempool eviction rules can alter mempool consistency across nodes or lead to unintended transaction retention and memory pressure.

scope_notes: Deletes test/functional/mempool_expiry.py and updates existing tests (interface_usdt_mempool.py, wallet_resendwallettransactions.py) and mempool fuzz targets to remove dependence on expiry.
summary: Removes time-based transaction expiry (-mempoolexpiry) and deletes the entry_time multi-index from the mempool. Transactions will now only leave the mempool due to size limiting (-maxmempool), block inclusion, replacement, or conflict. The -mempoolexpiry startup argument is retained as a hidden no-op that logs an initialization warning if set.
